description: Baseline benchmark across all Go benchmarks with median per benchmark and geomean primary metric

asi.hypothesis: Establish stable baseline for all existing benchmarks before applying optimizations.
asi.baseline_observations: CLI parse/help benchmarks dominate geomean; NewString combines UUID generation and Base58 encode. EncodeBase58 allocates twice due external encoder plus string concatenation/padding; UUID7/FromTime allocate via crypto/rand.Int and math/big.

description: Replace math/big rand.Int UUID randomness with rand.Read and integer sub-ms precision

asi.hypothesis: Avoid crypto/rand.Int's math/big allocation path and float math while preserving UUIDv7 variant/version/output semantics.
asi.learned: Large general win: FromTime/UUID7 now zero-allocation; NewString dropped from 5 to 2 allocs because generation no longer allocates. rand.Read 8 bytes then masks variant bits is more direct and uniform for rand_b than previous big.Int path.

description: Direct fixed-width Base58 encoder reduced allocs but failed encode/decode/order tests; check output cap prevents pi crash on noisy failures

asi.hypothesis: Replacing base58.Encode with a one-allocation fixed-width encoder would reduce EncodeBase58/NewString allocations.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks fail massively: encoded strings do not match vectors, DecodeBase58 round trips fail, and lexicographic ordering breaks. The noisy TestEncodeDecode loop produced gigabytes of stdout, which is the concrete trigger for pi's Invalid string length crash.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the output-capped .auto/checks.sh; if revisiting direct Base58, implement canonical big-integer base conversion exactly or optimize around existing base58.Encode padding instead.
asi.pi_crash_cause: pi execCommand concatenates child stdout into a JS string; uncapped go test output exceeded V8 max string length at dist/core/exec.js stdout += data.toString().

description: Collapse CLI help output to a single constant WriteString and avoid fmt for generated ID newline

asi.hypothesis: printUsage currently performs many fmt.Println calls; replacing them with one constant WriteString preserves exact help text while avoiding repeated fmt dispatch and writes. Generated ID output may also avoid fmt overhead with WriteString.
asi.learned: The single constant usage write produced a very large general win for CLI help (about 8us to 0.39us). Generate path regressed in this sample likely due two direct writes/noise; primary geomean improved substantially because help was a dominant benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider testing whether generateUUID should use fmt.Println or a single write buffer rather than two WriteString calls; also optimize parseUUID output formatting/DecodeBase58 next.

description: Collapse parse output formatting into one Fprintf with shared time format constant

asi.hypothesis: parseUUID spends much of its time in many fmt.Print* calls and repeated parsing of the timestamp layout literal; one Fprintf with a shared layout constant should preserve exact CLI output while reducing dispatch and write overhead.
asi.learned: Large general win for CLI parse: BenchmarkParseUUID and BenchmarkMainParse dropped from ~5us to ~1.3us with unchanged allocation counts, confirming output call overhead dominated parse after DecodeBase58/time formatting.
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising areas: optimize DecodeBase58 allocation/path generally, or revisit generateUUID output to avoid the current two WriteString calls causing slower generate benchmarks.

description: Direct zero-allocation Base58 decode passed correctness but slowed primary geomean

asi.hypothesis: Avoid DecodeBase58's separator-removal string allocation and base58.Decode output allocation by decoding the 22 Base58 digits directly into a UUID with a lookup table, preserving valid input behavior and using the dependency only for invalid-character errors.
asi.rollback_reason: Although correctness checks passed and allocations dropped to zero for DecodeBase58, the per-digit base256 loop was much slower (DecodeBase58 ~137ns to ~249ns, EncodeDecode ~448ns to ~536ns), increasing primary geomean versus the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not use the naive direct decode algorithm. If revisiting decode, consider a faster chunked/base conversion or focus on reducing parse/output allocations elsewhere.

description: Restore fmt.Printf for generated ID output after two WriteString calls proved slower

asi.hypothesis: The prior CLI help optimization also changed generateUUID to two os.Stdout.WriteString calls; despite fewer allocations, two interface method calls/writes may be slower than the original single fmt.Printf. Restoring fmt.Printf should improve generate benchmarks without changing output.
asi.learned: Restoring fmt.Printf improved GenerateUUID/MainGenerate substantially versus the current best sample (about 1.25us to 0.93-0.98us) and improved primary geomean to ~404.7 despite one extra allocation in the CLI generate path.
asi.next_action_hint: Try a single WriteString(base58String+"\n") or preallocated []byte write as alternatives to see if single syscall/write with less fmt overhead can beat fmt.Printf while preserving output.

description: Use one WriteString call with appended newline for generated ID output

asi.hypothesis: A single os.Stdout.WriteString(base58String+"\n") should preserve exact generate output while avoiding fmt.Printf overhead and avoiding the two separate writes that previously regressed generate performance.
asi.learned: Single WriteString with concatenated newline improved GenerateUUID/MainGenerate versus restored fmt.Printf and reduced allocations back to two; primary geomean improved to ~396.5 despite small noise in encode metrics.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider a zero-extra-allocation single os.Stdout.Write over a stack [24]byte built from the encoded string plus newline, or focus on EncodeBase58 allocation count.

description: Implement correct direct fixed-width Base58 encoder with one string allocation

asi.hypothesis: A correct direct Base58 encoder can preserve the exact 22-character padded hqid7 format while avoiding base58.Encode's intermediate result allocation and the padding/separator concatenation allocations.
asi.learned: The corrected little-endian base58 conversion passed the full high-coverage encode/order tests and reduced EncodeBase58/NewString/GenerateUUID allocations to one. This contrasts with the earlier failed fixed-width encoder; the key fix was building little-endian base58 digits and reversing them into a padded raw buffer.
asi.next_action_hint: Next explore small encode micro-optimizations (combine raw/out buffers, avoid copy loops) or parse output allocation reductions; avoid the previously discarded naive direct decoder.

description: Fill final Base58 output buffer directly instead of using raw buffer and copy

asi.hypothesis: Avoid the intermediate raw [22]byte and two copy calls in EncodeBase58 by initializing the final [23]byte output with padding and writing reversed base58 digits around the separator directly.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean was slightly worse than the current best (381.09 vs 380.69). EncodeBase58 and NewString were marginally slower, likely because the extra branch/index mapping in the digit placement loop outweighed removing raw buffer copies.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler raw+copy encoder. Future encode attempts should target the base conversion loop rather than final buffer assembly, or improve parse/generate paths.

description: Format parse output into a stack byte buffer with append helpers

asi.hypothesis: Replacing parseUUID's fmt.Fprintf and time.Format string creation with AppendFormat/strconv.Append* into a stack byte buffer should preserve exact CLI output while avoiding formatting allocations and reflection overhead.
asi.learned: Large general parse win: ParseUUID/MainParse dropped from ~1.3us and 10 allocations to ~0.88us and 1 allocation. The remaining allocation is likely DecodeBase58's separator removal/base58 decode path or os.File.Write escape of the buffer.
asi.next_action_hint: Next investigate whether DecodeBase58 can remove only the separator allocation while retaining dependency speed, or reduce the final parse buffer/write allocation.

description: Specialize fixed-width binary and hex append helpers for parse output

asi.hypothesis: The generic appendFixedBase helper divides by a dynamic base for binary and hex parse output. Specialized bit-shift based appendBitsFixed and appendHexFixed should preserve exact formatting while reducing parse formatting overhead.
asi.learned: Primary geomean improved slightly to ~351.2 and ParseUUID improved to ~860ns. MainParse regressed in this sample, but the overall primary metric improved and allocations stayed at one. Gains are small and likely near noise; future confirmation may be useful.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue with broader optimizations: investigate faster safe DecodeBase58 paths or reduce generate/output overhead. Avoid relying heavily on this small parse-helper gain without more runs if subsequent noise contradicts it.

description: Implement fast fixed-width Base58 decoder using uint32 limbs

asi.hypothesis: A fixed-width hqid7 decoder can mirror mr-tron/base58's uint32-limb algorithm without allocating the separator-stripped string, rune slice, output slice, or intermediate buffers. Because hqid7 input is always exactly 22 Base58 digits plus separator, the low 128 bits map directly to the final four limbs while preserving valid decode behavior and matching dependency-style invalid digit errors.
asi.learned: This is a large general win: DecodeBase58 dropped to ~87ns and zero allocations, EncodeDecode to ~362ns and one allocation, and parse paths became zero-allocation. Unlike the earlier naive byte-array decoder, uint32 limbs keep the conversion loop small and fast.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider micro-optimizing the decoder further by unrolling six limb updates or removing fmt imports with custom errors only if invalid-error text remains acceptable; also revisit EncodeBase58 base conversion loop.

description: Unroll fixed-width Base58 decoder limb multiplication loop

asi.hypothesis: DecodeBase58 always updates exactly six uint32 limbs for each of 22 digits, so unrolling the inner limb loop should reduce loop overhead and bounds checks while preserving the same overflow checks and error behavior.
asi.learned: Unrolling the six-limb multiply/add loop improved DecodeBase58 from ~87ns to ~69ns and EncodeDecode from ~362ns to ~341ns. Primary geomean improved despite some noise/regression in unrelated generate metrics.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider further decoder micro-optimizations such as processing the two digit ranges without the separator branch, but avoid duplicating too much code unless benchmark confirms a clear win.

description: Split Base58 decode loop around separator to remove per-digit branch

asi.hypothesis: DecodeBase58 always has a separator at index 9; splitting the loop into [0:9] and [10:23] removes a branch from each digit while preserving validation order and error behavior.
asi.learned: Primary geomean improved to ~304. DecodeBase58 improved modestly (~69ns to ~66ns), but this run also showed broad favorable noise across UUID/generate/help; the decode-specific improvement is plausible but smaller than the primary delta suggests.
asi.next_action_hint: Potential next decoder cleanup: factor duplicated digit body only if inlining preserves speed, or optimize UUID construction/direct byte stores. Also consider rerunning current state later to confirm broad-noise contribution.

description: Return decoded UUID via composite literal instead of binary.BigEndian stores

asi.hypothesis: Constructing the decoded UUID with a composite literal from the four uint32 limbs may avoid binary.BigEndian.PutUint32 call overhead at the end of DecodeBase58.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean regressed versus current best (306.81 vs 303.99). DecodeBase58 itself worsened from ~66ns to ~71ns, suggesting the compiler's BigEndian stores are already optimal or the composite literal adds overhead.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep binary.BigEndian.PutUint32 for UUID assembly. Future decoder experiments should focus on digit processing, overflow checks, or valid-path error branch structure rather than final UUID construction.

description: Try big-endian high-water fixed Base58 encoder loop

asi.hypothesis: A corrected big-endian/high-water Base58 encode loop like mr-tron/base58's stack algorithm might avoid the little-endian reverse/raw fill work while preserving the exact fixed-width padded output.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean regressed versus the current best (320.0 vs 304.0) and EncodeBase58 slowed materially (~262ns best sample to ~297ns). The high-water loop is correct but slower than the existing little-endian encoder for this fixed 16-byte input.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the little-endian encoder. Future encode work should target reducing divisions/modulo or special-casing by general input structure, not the big-endian high-water formulation.

description: Use 256-entry Base58 decode lookup to remove high-bit fast-path branch

asi.hypothesis: Expanding the Base58 decode lookup table to cover all byte values lets the valid fast path index directly without checking c > 127 before every lookup, while still returning the same high-bit invalid digit error when the decoded value is zero.
asi.learned: Correctness checks passed and DecodeBase58 improved to ~62ns with zero allocations; broad benchmark sample also improved the primary geomean to ~288.4. This is a general valid-path branch reduction, not benchmark-specific.

description: Encode Base58 with repeated division of uint32 limbs

asi.hypothesis: For a fixed 16-byte UUID, repeated division of four 32-bit limbs by 58 should need fewer divisions than the byte-by-byte base conversion loop while preserving canonical fixed-width Base58 output for every UUID.
asi.learned: Large general encode win: EncodeBase58 dropped from ~246ns to ~82ns and NewString/generate/encode-decode improved accordingly. Tests including exhaustive order/roundtrip checks passed, confirming the limb division output matches the original format.

description: Fill final Base58 output buffer directly for limb encoder

asi.hypothesis: With the new limb encoder, writing Base58 digits directly into the final 23-byte buffer might avoid the raw buffer plus two copies.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean worsened versus the current best and EncodeBase58/NewString slowed. The per-digit separator-index branch appears more expensive than copying the 22-byte raw buffer.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the raw buffer plus copy assembly. Future encode work should target the division loop or direct string construction without per-digit branches.

description: Call crypto/rand Reader.Read directly for UUID randomness

asi.hypothesis: Calling crypto/rand.Reader.Read directly might avoid helper overhead in rand.Read for the 8 random UUID bytes.
asi.rollback_reason: It regressed primary metric and introduced one allocation on every UUID generation path, likely from interface method call/escape behavior. rand.Read is better optimized here.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep rand.Read. Future UUID generation work should focus on timestamp arithmetic or output composition, not direct Reader.Read.

description: Manually store UUID timestamp field bytes instead of binary.BigEndian.PutUint64

asi.hypothesis: Manual byte stores for the first UUIDv7 64-bit field might avoid binary.BigEndian.PutUint64 overhead in FromTime/UUID7.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary metric regressed and FromTime/UUID7 got slower; the standard BigEndian store is optimized better than explicit byte assignments here.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep binary.BigEndian.PutUint64 in FromTime. Timestamp arithmetic or random-read costs are more relevant than store mechanics.

description: Format CLI parse timestamps with specialized append helper

asi.hypothesis: The CLI parse output uses a fixed timestamp layout; appending numeric date/time fields and the zone name directly should avoid time.AppendFormat's general formatter while preserving exact output, with fallback to time.AppendFormat for years outside 0..9999 and numeric-zone handling matching Go's MST layout.
asi.learned: Parse benchmarks improved substantially (~740ns to ~550-590ns) with zero allocations retained. The helper preserves general behavior for ordinary named zones and falls back for unusual years; empty zone names now emit +HHMM to match time.Format.

description: Try two-limb Base58 encoder with bits.Div64

asi.hypothesis: Representing the UUID as two uint64 limbs and using bits.Div64 for the low limb might halve the number of divisions in EncodeBase58 versus four uint32 limbs.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness passed, but EncodeBase58 slowed significantly (~82ns to ~120ns); bits.Div64/software 128-bit division is more expensive than four compiler-optimized constant 64-bit divisions by 58 on this platform.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the four-uint32-limb encoder. Avoid bits.Div64 for this fixed small divisor unless a future platform-specific benchmark shows otherwise.

description: Decode Base58 directly into four UUID limbs

asi.hypothesis: Because hqid7 input is fixed to 22 Base58 digits and the original decoder kept only the low 16 decoded bytes, DecodeBase58 can maintain only four uint32 UUID limbs and discard carry above 128 bits instead of updating six limbs and checking unreachable overflow conditions.
asi.learned: DecodeBase58 improved from ~63ns to ~56ns and encode-decode/parse improved. Correctness checks passed; 22 Base58 digits cannot exceed the old six-limb overflow thresholds, so removed overflow errors were not reachable for length-valid inputs.

description: Use two uint64 limbs with bits.Mul64 for Base58 decode

asi.hypothesis: For decoding, modulo-2^128 arithmetic can be represented as two uint64 limbs; multiplying the low limb by 58 with bits.Mul64 and carrying into the high limb should require much less work than four uint32 limb updates while preserving the low 128 decoded bits.
asi.learned: Very large decode win: DecodeBase58 fell from ~56ns to ~21ns, improving encode-decode and parse paths. This is safe for fixed 22-digit hqid7 inputs because the original decoder truncated to the low 16 bytes.

description: Attempt branchless Add64 carry in Base58 decoder but introduced short-declaration shadowing

asi.hypothesis: Replacing the overflow branch after loProd+digit with bits.Add64 might make decode branchless and faster.
asi.rollback_reason: The initial implementation used `lo, carry :=` inside loop bodies, which shadowed the outer lo and failed to compile as the inner lo was unused.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry with a carry variable declared outside the loops and `lo, carry = bits.Add64(...)` assignments, then benchmark.

description: Use bits.Add64 for branchless Base58 decode carry

asi.hypothesis: bits.Add64 can replace the rare overflow comparison after adding the Base58 digit to the low limb, making the decode update more branchless.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks passed, but primary geomean was slightly worse than current best and DecodeBase58 was marginally slower. The compiler's compare/conditional increment is already optimal here or the Add64 intrinsic adds overhead.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simple `lo = loProd + digit; if lo < loProd { loCarry++ }` decode carry handling.

description: Inline MustUUID7 logic in NewString

asi.hypothesis: Inlining MustUUID7's error handling directly in NewString might avoid an extra function call on the hot NewString path.
asi.rollback_reason: The change passed correctness but primary geomean worsened slightly and NewString did not improve, indicating the compiler already inlines or optimizes the existing MustUUID7 call adequately.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep NewString delegating to EncodeBase58(MustUUID7()). Focus on larger costs such as CLI writes/time formatting or Base58 encode.

description: Factor UUID generation through unix-nanoseconds helper

asi.hypothesis: Having UUID7 call a helper with time.Now().UnixNano directly may avoid passing a full time.Time through FromTime while preserving FromTime behavior via the same helper.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness passed, but primary metric was slightly worse than current best; UUID7 did not improve and FromTime regressed. The extra helper/inlining tradeoff is not beneficial.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep UUID7 delegating to FromTime(time.Now()). Timestamp helper factoring is not worth pursuing without a clearer compiler benefit.

description: Reduce CLI parse stack output buffer size

asi.hypothesis: The parse output buffer is stack-allocated and zeroed; reducing it from 512 to 320 bytes should still cover normal parse output while lowering stack zeroing/copy overhead, with append still preserving correctness if an unusual long zone name requires growth.
asi.learned: Small parse-path win with zero allocations retained for the benchmark output (about 299 bytes in the local environment). This is a general buffer sizing improvement rather than output-specific logic.

description: Encode Base58 two digits at a time with base 58 squared

asi.hypothesis: Since hqid7's fixed Base58 width is 22 characters, the encoder can divide the 128-bit value by 58^2 and emit two digits per iteration, halving the number of limb-division passes while preserving padded output.
asi.learned: Large encode win: EncodeBase58 fell from ~82ns to ~57ns, NewString and generate paths improved, and exhaustive encode/order checks passed. Pairwise base-58 chunks are a clean general fixed-width optimization.

description: Encode Base58 three digits at a time with base 58 cubed

asi.hypothesis: The fixed 22-character width can also be filled from the right in base 58^3 chunks (seven full 3-digit groups plus one leading digit), further reducing 128-bit division passes versus 58^2.
asi.learned: Another large encode win: EncodeBase58 dropped from ~57ns to ~43ns and NewString to ~152ns. The top partial group is safe because 22 Base58 digits leave a one-character leading group; exhaustive tests passed.

description: Encode Base58 four digits at a time with base 58^4 chunks

asi.hypothesis: Using base 58^4 chunks reduces the fixed-width encoder to six 128-bit division passes (five full 4-character groups plus a two-character leading group), which may beat the 58^3 encoder despite a larger divisor.
asi.learned: Base58^4 improved EncodeBase58 further (~43ns to ~41ns) and helped generate/NewString. The gain is smaller than prior chunking but correctness checks passed, so 4-digit chunks are the current best encoding strategy.

description: Try Base58 encoder with 58^5 chunks

asi.hypothesis: Base 58^5 chunks reduce the encoder to five division passes, which might overcome the larger divisor and extra digit extraction for each chunk.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness passed, but primary geomean and EncodeBase58 were slightly worse than the 58^4 encoder. The larger divisor and 5-digit extraction outweigh the reduced pass count on this platform.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep 58^4 chunks as the best observed encoder chunk size; avoid larger chunk sizes unless using a different division strategy.

description: Use Base58 pair lookup table for 58^4 chunk digit extraction

asi.hypothesis: For 58^4 chunks, rem can be split into two base-58 pairs; a small 3364-entry pair table should replace several per-chunk /58 and %58 operations with two table lookups while preserving all outputs.
asi.learned: EncodeBase58 improved from ~41ns to ~37ns with a modest 6.5KB lookup table initialized at package startup. This is a general chunk-digit extraction optimization.

description: Try 58^5 encoding with pair-table digit extraction

asi.hypothesis: The previous 58^5 encoder lost to 58^4 partly due digit extraction; reusing the 58^2 pair table for the low/middle digit pairs may make five-digit chunks competitive.
asi.learned: Primary geomean improved very slightly, although EncodeBase58 itself was a bit slower than the 58^4 pair-table sample. This keep is likely noise-sensitive; consider rerunning or reverting to 58^4 if subsequent runs show no durable primary gain.
